profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting for a near-final 28-page white paper titled 'Sonification Report: Status of the Field and Research Agenda,' being prepared for limited external circulation to an NSF program officer, two advisory-panel members, and one senior interdisciplinary methods reviewer. The document already argues that sonification should be recognized as a legitimate research area and proposes a national research agenda spanning perception/cognition, tool development, and design/application. The meeting agenda is to evaluate whether the current draft is ready for this circulation round, check whether the report adequately represents the field and its interdisciplinary character, and decide what revisions are needed in the recommendations on workshops, conferences, a journal, and curriculum. The expected outcome is a shared decision on whether to send the next draft this week and a short revision list that does not appear to reopen the core structure of the report.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: research program framing, interdisciplinary initiative development, science policy writing
members.background: Maya has spent eight years converting emerging technical areas into fundable research roadmaps for federal and foundation audiences, with earlier training in cognitive science and public policy and repeated experience preparing briefing-ready white papers for external stakeholders.
members.private_state: She wants this design review to end with approval for circulation because the paper is needed for an upcoming briefing packet, and she is mainly concerned that the report read as authoritative, coherent, and strategically useful rather than as a comprehensive scholarly treatment.
hidden_assumptions: A document can be 'ready to circulate' if its framing is polished and credible for a small external audience even when some scholarly detail and citation refinement are still pending.
A 'research agenda' in this context should identify priority themes, funding logic, and field-shaping directions rather than spell out lab-level methodological playbooks.
A 'representative' treatment of the field means one or two emblematic examples per major component that signal the category clearly without trying to map all of its internal variation.

To 'strengthen' recommendations such as workshops, conferences, and a journal mainly means sharpening the rationale, anticipated impact, and strategic case for support, not adding operational rollout steps.

members.name: Prof. Elias Romero
members.expertise: auditory display design, empirical evaluation, multimodal interaction, academic field building
members.background: Elias is a professor who has led sonification projects across scientific visualization, assistive interfaces, and perception studies, and he has served on interdisciplinary review panels where emerging areas were judged partly on whether their roadmaps showed methodological maturity and community infrastructure.
members.private_state: He wants the report to help legitimize sonification as a discipline in the eyes of skeptical researchers, and he worries that if it goes out too soon it will sound strategically persuasive but thin on what the field actually needs to build.
hidden_assumptions: A document is only 'ready to circulate' if outside experts could read it as substantively complete and not immediately see major gaps in examples, methodological grounding, or institutional recommendations.

A 'research agenda' should indicate enough about study types, validation expectations, tool capabilities, and infrastructure needs that readers can infer what concrete research programs ought to be supported.

A 'representative' treatment of the field means the examples span meaningful breadth within each component so readers can see the variance of methods, applications, and interdisciplinary approaches rather than a single emblematic case.

To 'strengthen' recommendations on workshops, conferences, and a journal means making the support path more concrete by indicating sequence, linkage, or mechanism, so the recommendations read as feasible designs rather than aspirational bullets.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss whether the draft is 'ready to circulate' this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'ready to circulate' means polished enough for limited external review by funders and advisors, with only light scholarly strengthening still possible afterward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'ready to circulate' means already robust enough that expert readers would not see any substantive weaknesses requiring meaningful revision.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase names a normal workflow milestone rather than an explicit quality standard, so both can sincerely say the draft is nearly ready while silently applying different thresholds for sufficiency.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree the 'research agenda' section should be tightened.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 uses 'research agenda' to mean a concise set of top-level national priorities and funding justifications for sonification as an emerging field.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 uses 'research agenda' to mean a more operational roadmap that still stays concise but signals needed study programs, evaluation frameworks, and tool infrastructure.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are accustomed to documents labeled 'research agenda,' and each version sounds compatible with the other's surface language of clarity and concision, so neither hears a need to define the genre explicitly.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the draft should use 'representative examples' to show the field.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'representative examples' means a small number of clean, emblematic cases—such as one multimodal display example and one tool-building example—that stand in for larger categories and keep the narrative efficient.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'representative examples' means a set of examples chosen to reflect the spread of the field—for instance, across perception studies, assistive applications, scientific data interpretation, and design methodology—so the reader sees real breadth.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The word 'representative' strongly implies adequacy to both of them, but in policy writing it often means emblematic while in scholarly framing it often means spanning variation; the same adjective therefore creates a convincing illusion of agreement.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to 'strengthen' the field-building recommendations
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree the recommendations on workshops, conferences, and a peer-reviewed journal should be 'strengthened.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes 'strengthened' means improving the prose around why these supports matter—e.g., adding sharper justification about recognition, coordination, and NSF's catalytic role—while keeping the recommendations high-level.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes 'strengthened' means adding light but concrete procedural structure—e.g., that workshops seed a recurring conference, which then supports a journal and shared curriculum development—so the recommendations imply an execution path.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both already endorse the same recommendations, 'strengthen' feels like a harmless refinement rather than a decision about the form of elaboration, so the hidden difference in expected revision type is easy to miss during a cooperative review.

turns.inner_thought: I want this meeting to end with a clear go decision. For this round, ready to circulate means polished enough for the NSF officer and the small advisory group to react to the framing, coherence, and strategic utility. We can still refine scholarly detail afterward if needed, but I do not want to reopen the paper.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. My goal today is pretty simple: confirm whether the current draft is ready to circulate this week and identify any final revisions we want before it goes out to the external readers.

turns.inner_thought: The overall frame is much better than it was, but I do not want this going out unless outside experts would see it as substantively complete. The research agenda still risks reading as high-level advocacy rather than a convincing account of what the field actually needs to build next.
turns.utterance: I think the overall framing is strong. My main hesitation is just making sure the research agenda is tightened before the draft circulates.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds manageable. The three-part structure is already doing the job, and I can reinforce credibility with a small set of clean, emblematic examples without expanding the document into a broad literature review. I need to keep this efficient and briefing-friendly.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. I do think the three-part structure is already working, and one thing we could do without adding much length is use a small set of representative examples to reinforce the field overview.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, examples would help, but they need to show real breadth within the field so readers see it is not just one style of work. I want multimodal systems, perceptual research, and different application areas visible enough that the field looks methodologically and practically grounded.
turns.utterance: I agree, representative examples would help. I’d just want to make sure they show multimodal work, perceptual research, and some application diversity so the field reads as broadly grounded.

turns.inner_thought: Fine as long as the agenda section stays concise and anchored in major national priorities and funding logic. I do not want it turning into a detailed methods roadmap or a catalog of study designs. The audience needs direction and rationale more than implementation detail.
turns.utterance: Yes, I’m comfortable refining the examples along those lines, as long as the research agenda stays crisp and remains focused on the major directions the report is recommending.

turns.inner_thought: Crisp is good, but it still has to signal what concrete research programs should exist. If it mentions evaluation frameworks, perceptual studies, and flexible tools, expert readers can infer methodological maturity instead of seeing only strategic language.
turns.utterance: I want it crisp too. I just think it should still indicate the kinds of evaluation frameworks, perceptual studies, and flexible tools the field needs next.

turns.inner_thought: Now I need to move us toward contained revisions. The community-building recommendations matter for the briefing packet because they show a credible field-shaping role, but strengthened should mean making the strategic case sharper, not designing an operational rollout.
turns.utterance: That’s helpful. On the community-building section, I do think the recommendations on workshops, conferences, and a peer-reviewed journal are important, and they should be strengthened in the next draft.

turns.inner_thought: Exactly. Those recommendations are right, but they need more visible structure so they read as feasible and mutually reinforcing. A clearer relationship among workshops, conference activity, and an eventual journal would make the field-building case feel real.
turns.utterance: Agreed. I’d strengthen them by making the relationship among the workshop series, conference community, and eventual journal a bit clearer.

turns.inner_thought: That still sounds like something I can absorb as framing language. I can sharpen why these supports matter for recognition, communication, and curriculum building without turning this section into a step-by-step plan.
turns.utterance: Yes, that sounds useful. I’d frame that as a brief sharpening of the case for why those supports matter for recognition, communication, and curriculum building.

turns.inner_thought: If the examples actually show breadth, the agenda signals needed programs and infrastructure, and the recommendations feel more coherent, then I would be comfortable. I still mean ready to circulate in the stronger sense, but these changes could get it there.
turns.utterance: Right. With stronger examples and a tightened agenda and recommendations, I’d feel good about circulation.

turns.inner_thought: Good, he is basically on board. I can treat this as confirmation that the draft is essentially ready now, with a quick refinement pass to incorporate examples and tighten wording. That keeps the schedule intact and avoids reopening structure.
turns.utterance: Great, then I’m hearing that the draft is essentially ready now, pending a quick refinement pass on the representative examples and some updates in the agenda and recommendations.

turns.inner_thought: I would describe the needed changes as more than cosmetic, but I can send targeted markup today and trust that the updates will be incorporated fully enough. If they are, the circulated version should read much stronger to outside readers.
turns.utterance: Yes, I can send markup later today on the examples, the agenda language, and the recommendation section so the circulated version is stronger for the outside readers.
